title: Hebrews Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 2.

questions.question: In Hebrews 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'we ought to give the more earnest heed' appears first in Hebrews 2:1.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 2:1, what should we give earnest heed to?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:1 states, 'Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 2:2 say was steadfast?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:2 mentions, 'For if the word spoken by angels was stedfast.'

questions.question: What received a just recompence of reward according to Hebrews 2:2?
options: The gifts of the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:2 states, 'and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reward.'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 2:3, how shall we escape?
options: If we neglect so great salvation
questions.correctAnswer: If we neglect so great salvation
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:3 asks, 'How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation?'

questions.question: Who first spoke the great salvation mentioned in Hebrews 2:3?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:3 states, 'which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord.'

questions.question: Who confirmed the message of salvation according to Hebrews 2:3?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:3 says it was 'confirmed unto us by them that heard him,' referring to the apostles.

questions.question: What does God bear witness to according to Hebrews 2:4?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:4 states, 'God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 2:4 mention as being given according to God's own will?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:4 lists 'signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost.'

questions.question: Who has the world to come not been put in subjection to, according to Hebrews 2:5?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:5 states, 'For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come.'

questions.question: What is man that God is mindful of him, according to Hebrews 2:6?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:6 references the question, 'What is man, that thou art mindful of him?' indicating his mortal nature.

questions.question: True or False: The text states that angels received a just recompense of reward.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:2 specifically refers to 'every transgression and disobedience' rather than angels.

questions.question: True or False: Signs and wonders are mentioned in Hebrews 2:4.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:4 clearly states that God bore witness with 'signs and wonders.'

questions.question: True or False: The world to come is put in subjection to mankind according to the text.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:5 states that 'the angels' have not been put in subjection to the world to come.

questions.question: True or False: The text mentions that the Holy Ghost is given according to God's will.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:4 includes 'gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will.'

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What position has God set man over according to Hebrews 2:7?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 2:7 states that God made man 'a little lower than the angels' and 'set him over the works of thy hands.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 2:3 promise will happen if someone gives earnest heed to the things which they have heard?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 2:3 warns that neglecting so great salvation could result in not escaping judgment.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 2:9, who was crowned with glory and honour?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 2:9 specifically states that 'we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour.'

questions.question: What is stated in Hebrews 2:5 about angels?
options: They are in subjection to the world to come
They do not have authority over the earth
questions.correctAnswer: They do not have authority over the earth
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 2:5 clarifies that 'unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 2:10 imply about the captain of salvation?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Hebrews 2:10 states that it was fitting for God to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 2:11, what is the relationship between Jesus and those who are sanctified?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 2:11 states, 'For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 2:12 say Jesus will do in the midst of the church?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Hebrews 2:12 states, 'I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee.'

questions.question: How does Hebrews 2:8 describe the current situation of all things in relation to man?
options: All things are under his feet
Some things are under his feet
questions.correctAnswer: All things are under his feet
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 2:8 states that 'Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet.'

questions.question: What is emphasized in Hebrews 2:1 regarding what we have heard?
options: To give earnest heed to it
questions.correctAnswer: To give earnest heed to it
questions.explanation: This is correct as Hebrews 2:1 urges us to 'give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard.'

questions.question: What crucial aspect of salvation is mentioned in Hebrews 2:3?
options: It was first spoken by the angels
It was first spoken by the Lord
It is only for the chosen
questions.correctAnswer: It was first spoken by the Lord
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 2:3 states that the great salvation 'which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord.'

questions.question: What does Hebrews 2:4 indicate about God's confirmation of the message?
options: It was confirmed by signs and wonders
It is only for the rich
questions.correctAnswer: It was confirmed by signs and wonders
questions.explanation: This is correct as Hebrews 2:4 mentions that 'God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders.'

questions.question: What is the nature of the world to come as mentioned in Hebrews 2:5?
options: It is not put in subjection to angels
questions.correctAnswer: It is not put in subjection to angels
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 2:5 states that 'unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come.'

questions.question: True or False: Jesus is ashamed to call those who are sanctified his brethren.
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 2:11 states that he is not ashamed to call them brethren.

questions.question: True or False: The message of salvation was confirmed by angels alone.
questions.explanation: This is correct as Hebrews 2:3-4 indicates that it was first spoken by the Lord and confirmed by signs, wonders, and gifts of the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: True or False: Only the angels are subject to God’s authority.
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 2:8 states that all things are put under man's feet, indicating a broader authority.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 2:13, whom does Jesus say He will put His trust in?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:13 states, 'And again, I will put my trust in him,' indicating Jesus trusts in 'him' as the correct answer.

questions.question: Hebrews 2:14 explains that Jesus took part in flesh and blood to accomplish what purpose?
options: To destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil
To become a prophet among men
questions.correctAnswer: To destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:14 explicitly states Jesus took part of flesh and blood 'that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil.'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 2:15, what does Jesus deliver those who were subject to bondage through fear of death from?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:15 says Jesus delivers 'them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.'

questions.question: Hebrews 2:16 clarifies that Jesus did not take on the nature of angels, but instead took on what?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:16 states, 'For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.'

questions.question: Why, according to Hebrews 2:17, was it necessary for Jesus to be made like His brethren?
options: To be a merciful and faithful high priest to make reconciliation for sins
questions.correctAnswer: To be a merciful and faithful high priest to make reconciliation for sins
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:17 explains Jesus 'might be a merciful and faithful high priest... to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.'

questions.question: What ability does Jesus have according to Hebrews 2:18 because He Himself suffered being tempted?
options: To succour them that are tempted
questions.correctAnswer: To succour them that are tempted
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:18 states, 'For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'succour' (Hebrews 2:18) mean?
options: To help or aid in time of need
questions.correctAnswer: To help or aid in time of need
questions.explanation: The Greek word translated 'succour' in Hebrews 2:18 is ἐπικουρέω (epikoureó), meaning 'to help or aid in time of need.'

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Hebrews 2:14-15 where Jesus shares flesh and blood to destroy the devil and free from bondage?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:14-15 uses typology by presenting Jesus' incarnation and death as fulfilling and destroying the power of the devil, foreshadowed in Old Testament themes.

questions.question: Hebrews 2:7 mentions man being made 'a little lower than the angels.' Which Psalm is this verse quoting?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:6-7 quotes Psalm 8:4-6, which speaks of man being made a little lower than angels and crowned with glory and honor.

questions.question: Hebrews 2:9 describes Jesus being crowned with glory and honor after suffering death. Which Old Testament figure is this concept linked to as the 'captain of salvation'?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:10 and 2:9 imply Jesus as the captain or leader of salvation, a concept foreshadowed by Moses who led Israel to deliverance, linking the typology of salvation.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Hebrews 2:13, where Jesus says 'I will put my trust in him'?
options: A declaration of praise in the church
questions.correctAnswer: A declaration of praise in the church
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:12 immediately precedes 2:13 and contains a declaration, 'I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee,' which leads into 2:13.

questions.question: Which theme from Hebrews 2:16 about Jesus taking on 'the seed of Abraham' is emphasized in other New Testament writings?
options: Jesus' solidarity with humanity and fulfillment of the Abrahamic promise
Jesus' role as a prophet to the Gentiles
Jesus' establishment of the Mosaic Law
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus' solidarity with humanity and fulfillment of the Abrahamic promise
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:16's emphasis on Jesus taking on 'the seed of Abraham' highlights His human solidarity and fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham, a theme echoed in Galatians 3:16.

questions.question: Hebrews 2:11 states that Jesus is not ashamed to call those sanctified his brethren. What Old Testament concept does this reflect?
options: The concept of the Messiah as the suffering servant
The concept of a royal priesthood among God's people
The concept of the covenant community as God's family
The concept of angels serving as mediators
questions.correctAnswer: The concept of the covenant community as God's family
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:11’s idea that Jesus calls sanctified believers 'brethren' echoes OT ideas of covenant community as God's family (e.g., Exodus 4:22).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is directly quoted in Hebrews 2:6-8 to discuss man's position relative to angels?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:6-8 quotes Psalm 8 to describe man's creation 'a little lower than the angels' and crowned with glory and honor.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 2:18 teaches that because Jesus was tempted, He is able to help those who are tempted.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:18 clearly states Jesus 'hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted,' confirming He can help those tempted.

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 2:3 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is a great and urgent gift first spoken by the Lord and confirmed by eyewitnesses
Salvation is attained by angelic mediation and laws
Salvation is a future promise only and not yet realized
Salvation is based on human works and obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is a great and urgent gift first spoken by the Lord and confirmed by eyewitnesses
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:3 emphasizes the greatness of salvation and its origin with the Lord, confirmed by those who heard Him directly.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 2:14 teach about Christ's incarnation and purpose?
options: Christ took on flesh and blood to destroy the devil who has power over death
Christ remained purely divine and did not share human nature
Christ came only to reveal divine mysteries, not to suffer death
Christ’s incarnation was symbolic, not literal
questions.correctAnswer: Christ took on flesh and blood to destroy the devil who has power over death
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:14 teaches that Christ shared in human nature so that through His death He might defeat the devil who holds the power of death.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 2:17 teach about Christ’s priesthood?
options: Christ had to be like His brethren to be a merciful and faithful high priest making reconciliation for sins
Christ’s priesthood is temporary and limited to the earthly temple
Christ’s priesthood does not involve mercy or faithfulness
Christ’s priesthood replaces the need for reconciliation
questions.correctAnswer: Christ had to be like His brethren to be a merciful and faithful high priest making reconciliation for sins
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:17 explains that Christ’s likeness to humanity qualifies Him to be a merciful and faithful high priest who makes atonement for sins.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 2:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:4 shows God’s sovereignty as He bears witness through signs, wonders, miracles, and gifts according to His will.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 2:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:11 demonstrates God’s attribute of communion or fellowship as Christ is not ashamed to call sanctified believers His brethren.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 2:7 connect to the broader biblical theme of humanity’s place in creation?
options: It recalls Psalm 8’s theme that humanity is crowned with glory and honor, just below angels
It denies any special status for humanity over animals
It teaches that angels are superior to humans in all respects
It focuses only on Christ’s status and not humanity’s
questions.correctAnswer: It recalls Psalm 8’s theme that humanity is crowned with glory and honor, just below angels
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:7 quotes Psalm 8, connecting humanity’s dignity and rank in creation as crowned with glory and honor just below angels.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 2:10 prepare for the New Testament theme of Christ’s perfecting work through suffering?
options: It shows that Christ’s sufferings perfect Him as the captain of salvation, enabling believers’ glorification
It teaches that Christ was perfect from eternity and suffered no growth
It disconnects suffering from salvation entirely
It limits Christ’s suffering to physical pain without spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that Christ’s sufferings perfect Him as the captain of salvation, enabling believers’ glorification
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:10 explains that it was fitting for Christ to be perfected through suffering to lead many sons into glory, linking suffering and salvation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Hebrews 2:8 and 2:9 teach about Christ’s exaltation and humanity’s role?
options: Christ was made lower than angels to die but is now crowned with glory and honor, fulfilling humanity’s intended dominion
Christ remains permanently lower than angels without exaltation
Humans have already fully received dominion over all things apart from Christ
Christ’s death is unrelated to His position relative to angels
questions.correctAnswer: Christ was made lower than angels to die but is now crowned with glory and honor, fulfilling humanity’s intended dominion
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:8-9 shows Christ’s humility in death and His exaltation crowned with glory, accomplishing what humanity was intended to receive.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 2:16 and 2:17 teach about Christ’s incarnation and priesthood?
options: Christ took on the seed of Abraham, not angelic nature, to be a merciful and faithful high priest reconciling humanity
Christ took on the nature of angels to be a priest
Christ’s priesthood depends solely on divine nature without human likeness
Christ’s incarnation was unnecessary for His priestly role
questions.correctAnswer: Christ took on the seed of Abraham, not angelic nature, to be a merciful and faithful high priest reconciling humanity
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:16-17 teaches that Christ assumed human nature descended from Abraham to fulfill His role as merciful and faithful high priest.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 2:13 and 2:12 teach about Christ’s relationship with believers?
options: Christ identifies with believers as brethren and publicly declares God’s name among them
Christ remains distant and separate from believers
Christ’s relationship with believers is symbolic only
Christ’s trust is in believers rather than God
questions.correctAnswer: Christ identifies with believers as brethren and publicly declares God’s name among them
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:12-13 shows Christ calling believers brethren and expressing trust while praising God in their midst.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Hebrews 2:1-4 teaches that salvation is uncertain and unconfirmed. What does this passage actually teach?
options: The passage teaches the necessity of paying earnest heed to the confirmed word of salvation, witnessed by signs and wonders
The passage denies any confirmation of salvation
The passage teaches salvation is guaranteed regardless of heed
The passage emphasizes salvation by angels rather than Christ
questions.correctAnswer: The passage teaches the necessity of paying earnest heed to the confirmed word of salvation, witnessed by signs and wonders
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:1-4 warns against neglecting salvation which was confirmed by those who heard Christ and God’s testimony through miracles.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 2:15 teach about the effect of Christ’s death on believers?
options: Christ’s death delivers believers from lifelong bondage to the fear of death
Christ’s death has no impact on human fear
Believers remain subject to death’s fear despite Christ’s death
The fear of death is unrelated to spiritual bondage
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s death delivers believers from lifelong bondage to the fear of death
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:15 states that Christ’s death frees those who were all their life subject to bondage through fear of death.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 2:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:18 shows Christ’s empathy as He is able to help those being tempted because He Himself suffered temptation.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 2:1 teach about the believer’s response to revelation?
options: Believers must give earnest heed to the revealed word to avoid losing it
Believers are free to ignore revelation without consequence
Revelation is unclear and cannot be heeded
Only angels need to heed revelation
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must give earnest heed to the revealed word to avoid losing it
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:1 commands believers to pay more earnest attention to the word heard to prevent neglecting it.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 2:5 teach about the subjection of the world to come?
options: The world to come has not been put under the authority of angels
Angels have full authority over the world to come
The world to come is irrelevant to Christian doctrine
Humans have no role in the world to come
questions.correctAnswer: The world to come has not been put under the authority of angels
questions.explanation: Hebrews 2:5 states that God has not subjected the world to come to angels, implying a different order of authority.
